entities.summary:
Peter of Tarentaise was a Cistercian monk who served as the archbishop of Tarentaise from 1141 until his death in 1174.

Born into a prominent family, Peter was educated at the University of Paris, where he studied theology and philosophy.

In 1141, he was appointed archbishop of Tarentaise, a position he held until his death, and played a key role in shaping the church's response to the Crusades.

As a prominent figure in the Cistercian Order, Peter was known for his advocacy of monastic reform and his efforts to promote the interests of the church in the region.
